tagline: Seven miles down from the crest, against the bicycles.
intro: At Saratoga Gap, about 2,608 feet up on the summit of the Santa Cruz Mountains, a vista point gives a somewhat obstructed view of the Bay Area. From there Highway 9 descends east as Congress Springs Road, seven miles down to Saratoga Village, the same grade bicycles climb in numbers on weekend mornings. In Saratoga it turns southeast as Saratoga-Los Gatos Road and runs on through Monte Sereno to Los Gatos.
The town at the bottom has answered to McCarthysville, Toll Gate and Bank Mills. In 1865 it became Saratoga, after the New York spa whose waters its own mineral springs resembled.

moments.title: Saratoga Gap
moments.text: The road's highest point, where Highway 9 meets Skyline Boulevard and motorcyclists gather in the junction parking lot through the summer months.

moments.title: Hakone Gardens
moments.text: A Japanese garden built from 1917 to 1929 as a summer retreat, where Madama Butterfly had its West Coast premiere in 1923.

moments.title: Los Gatos
moments.text: Since 1978 the Great Race has sent more than 1,000 runners between Saratoga and Los Gatos near the end of April, into a town named for its cougars and bobcats.
